sampling_model.design: Observational two-period binary panel with exact inversion of the sixteen-cell law.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units drawn from the population law \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The binary predetermined covariate \(X_t\) is not randomized. Initial assignment and the feedback distribution of \(X_2\) after \((X_1,Y_1)\) may depend arbitrarily on \(u\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell is positive. The weak latent model permits zero assignment or feedback probabilities; the strict latent model requires almost-everywhere positivity, with no numerical lower bound. Observed-cell positivity alone does not imply the strict latent condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell law is estimated by multinomial frequencies. Whole-set inversion uses simultaneous Clopper--Pearson marginal intervals, while fixed-slope endpoint estimation projects frequencies onto the relevant attainable affine hull.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 1 verifies membership by feasibility of a finite- or infinite-dimensional linear program.
Theorem 3.1 characterizes the identified set by conditional moment equalities with generalized moments in a truncated Stieltjes cone.
Theorem 1 characterizes all feedback and heterogeneity robust moment conditions for the common parameter.
The main theorem replaces a latent distribution by a finite-dimensional identification-equivalent distribution for discrete covariates.
The paper constructs root-\(n\) outer bounds and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for average-effect identified sets.

body.tldr: For a two-period binary logit panel with a predetermined binary covariate, continuous unrestricted heterogeneity, and heterogeneity-dependent initial assignment and feedback, the model-generated joint slope--APE fibers equal finite quartic Stieltjes feasibility sets. Eight coupled response-type measures preserve one unconditional heterogeneity law and reconstruct legal sequential kernels without a cross-world independence assumption. The weak certificate has fifty-six variables with eight \(3\times3\) and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; strict almost-everywhere assignment and feedback positivity has sixty-four variables and eight further \(6\times6\) common-range blocks. Downstream results give sharp fixed-slope endpoint programs with separate attainment tests, terminating algebraic membership and projection, exact multinomial whole-set coverage, and pointwise endpoint consistency only at relative-interior attainable laws. Uniform inference at rank-changing boundary laws and joint consistency through \(c=1\) remain open.

project_justification.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham characterize the sharp unrestricted-feedback model by an infinite-dimensional continuous-heterogeneity program and compute with support grids. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell develop truncated-Stieltjes tools for a different conditional structure, but do not reconstruct a separately unknown heterogeneity-dependent feedback kernel from one unconditional mixing law.
project_justification.niche: At two periods, an artificial product coupling of the two feedback-coordinate marginals creates eight joint response types without asserting cross-world independence. The binary-logit path likelihoods share a positive quartic denominator, so five bounded generalized moments per type suffice; common Hankel range is exactly what upgrades separate open-half-line representability to a shared finite positive-node support with every type weight positive.
project_justification.fill: The note defines weak and strict identified fibers from legal sequential models and proves two-sided maps between those models, eight response-type measures, and finite Stieltjes lifts. The reverse map constructs one unconditional probability law and normalized measurable initial and feedback kernels. The same exact cone supports sharp endpoint and attainment formulas, algebraic decision procedures, conservative exact multinomial set inversion, and fixed-slope relative-interior consistency.

body.related_work: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1 and Sections 5.1--5.3, provide the sharp continuous-heterogeneity unrestricted-feedback program and its support-grid implementation. The exact-feedback-cone theorem gives a two-sided finite representation of the same weak legal fiber and of the explicitly strengthened strict fiber. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026), Theorems 3.1--3.2, provide rational-mixture and truncated-Stieltjes ideas, but their model does not contain the separately unknown unrestricted feedback kernel reconstructed here. Curto and Fialkow (1991) and Bayer and Teichmann (2002) provide classical moment and finite-atomic substrate for singular open-half-line faces. Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2026) study feedback-robust moment equalities, while Gu, Russell, and Stringham (2026) use finite latent-cell enumeration for discrete-outcome index models; neither result supplies this continuous-logit legal-kernel equivalence. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) and Pakel and Weidner (2026) motivate, but do not solve, the remaining rank-changing inference problem. Arellano and Carrasco (2003) provide the predetermined-children labor-participation design that can consume the exact bounds.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The strict common-support proof is existential and does not provide an efficient atom-extraction algorithm. Real quantifier elimination terminates for algebraic inputs but carries no polynomial complexity or numerical-stability guarantee. A closed lifted PSD set can have a nonclosed linear image, so fixed-slope infima and suprema need separate endpoint-attainment tests. Relative-interior convex continuity does not extend automatically to attainable boundary laws, changes of Hankel rank, or the observable-map rank loss at \(c=1\).
body.honest_scope: The primitive targets are the model-generated weak and strict fibers. The proved contribution is their exact finite-certificate equivalence, including forward joint-response construction, reverse legal-kernel reconstruction, and the common-support certificate required for strict positivity. The note also delivers sharp fixed-slope endpoints with separate inclusion tests, algebraic membership and projection, a direct conservative exact multinomial whole-set inversion, and pointwise endpoint consistency for fixed \(c\) at relative-interior attainable laws. It imposes no support grid, latent density, tail moment, or numerical overlap margin. Boundary-uniform inference, continuity at strictly positive relative-boundary laws, joint consistency through \(c=1\), efficient certified extraction, arbitrary \(T\), restricted feedback dynamics, and multinomial outcomes remain outside the proved scope.
body.interpretation: The finite cone is an identifying map for the independently defined causal slope--APE fiber, not a regression estimand or a discretized outer approximation. Weak feasibility permits type measures with different supports. Strict feasibility is stronger: the common-range blocks certify a representation on one positive-node set with every response type receiving positive weight, which is exactly what makes all reconstructed initial and feedback probabilities positive almost everywhere.
